title: Ultrasound texture model to diagnose fibromyalgia

answers.study/department: Toronto Rehabilitation Institute, MSK/pain specialty outpatient clinic. Division of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (University of Toronto) and IBBME for the image analysis.
answers.study/summary: Secondary analysis of upper trapezius ultrasound videos collected under study 15-9488 (recruitment completed Sept 6, 2019) from fibromyalgia patients and age-matched healthy controls. We extract 88 texture features from muscle regions of interest and fit an elastic net regularized logistic regression to tell FM from healthy muscle, with nested cross-validation and an 80/20 holdout.
answers.classification/question: Can texture features from B-mode ultrasound of the upper trapezius discriminate fibromyalgia from healthy muscle (above 70% accuracy), does regularization help, and does the holdout set confirm the cross-validated performance?
answers.classification/cohort/population: Participants of 15-9488, aged 20 to 65: patients meeting the 2016 FM criteria with chronic widespread pain and no myofascial trigger points, and age-matched healthy controls with no past medical history.
answers.classification/cohort/dateRationale: Everyone enrolled in 15-9488, from its opening to the end of recruitment.
answers.classification/cohort/exclusionsWhy: Videos that fail the quality check (intensity, contrast, visible muscle fibres) are dropped, we expect under 15%. The age range is the original study's.
answers.classification/sources/sourceDetails: Study 15-9488 (CAPCR 15-9488), Dr. Kumbhare's lab at Toronto Rehab: upper trapezius ultrasound videos (Sonosite X-porte, one 10-second sweep per side), plus group, age and sex from the study forms.
answers.identifiability/fields: Study ID, group (FM or healthy), age, sex, side, and the ultrasound videos. Age and sex describe the groups and check the age matching. No names, MRNs or dates of birth in the analysis files.
answers.identifiability/lessIdentifiableWhy: The key stays with the original study so we can honour a participant's request to withdraw their data before publication, which the consent promised.
answers.identifiability/reidentification: Files named by study ID only. The key is a separate file on the PI's UHN drive. Only aggregate model results are published.
answers.handling/storage/access: Videos and the key on the Toronto Rehab research drive, access limited to the four study team members. Processing in MATLAB on a UHN lab workstation, encrypted, UHN login.
answers.handling/results/incidental: The videos are analyzed as texture features, nobody reads them clinically. If something clearly abnormal is noticed, Dr. Kumbhare reviews it and follows up through the clinic.
answers.resources/overlap: Our earlier myofascial pain syndrome classifier used the same ultrasound protocol on the trapezius. Different participants and a different question.

weaknesses: AI not declared: digital/ai/used false, but the study trains an elastic net classifier in MATLAB's Statistics and Machine Learning Toolbox as a diagnostic aid (p. 9-10), so the AI questions and the AI Hub intake are skipped.
Undeclared sharing: handling/leaving/otherUses 'none' and leaves 'no', while the protocol says the datasets will be available from the corresponding author on reasonable request (p. 13).

screening.summary: A small, consented secondary use of the team's own ultrasound data, kept inside UHN. Two answers don't match the protocol: the classifier is machine learning but AI is marked as not used, and the protocol offers the datasets on request while the form declares no other use. The videos themselves may carry identifiers.

assessments.summary: The study develops a machine-learned diagnostic classifier on participant images, which is AI development under UHN's governance, though it runs entirely on a local workstation.

comments.text: AI is marked as not used, but the study trains an elastic net regularized classifier on the participants' ultrasound images, aimed at computer-aided diagnosis of fibromyalgia. That is model development on study data, so the AI questions (use, where it runs, training, phase, governance) should be answered.
comments.suggestion: Answer yes, development phase, local processing, data used for training, and confirm the AI governance documents were read.
comments.quote: construct and train an elastic net regularized logistic regression model on the dataset using the binary class labels

assessments.summary: Nothing leaves UHN during the analysis, but the protocol commits to sharing the datasets on request after it, which the form doesn't declare.

comments.text: The protocol says the datasets will be available from the corresponding author on reasonable request, but the form says no other use and nothing leaving UHN. The consent under 15-9488 may not cover sharing, and the videos are not anonymized.
comments.suggestion: Either remove the statement or declare sharing, limit it to the extracted texture features (not the videos), check it against the original consent, and put it under an agreement.
comments.quote: The datasets used and/or analyzed during the study will be available from the corresponding author upon reasonable request.

assessments.summary: Coded data with a team-held key, justified by the withdrawal promise in the consent. Reasonable for a small consented cohort, with one practical gap.

comments.text: Ultrasound exports often carry the patient name or ID and the exam date, burned into the frame or in the file metadata. The form doesn't say whether the Sonosite videos were exported without them.
comments.suggestion: Confirm the videos are free of on-screen and metadata identifiers, or crop to the region of interest and strip metadata before analysis.

assessments.summary: Training runs in MATLAB on a UHN workstation and no data goes to an external service, so the risk is low. Once AI use is declared, the model training still needs the AI Hub intake.
